about.text: Shared Sidebar, imported by every page with its active item. Theme = HeroUI v3 dark tokens, Plus Jakarta Sans, as in internal/portal-pro. Example deployment: a support desk whose manager triages tickets and spawns worker threads.

Linear's project page: main column (goal, properties, Waiting on you, Latest update, composer), right rail (Milestones, Progress, Workers, Activity).
Pro: Widget, ChatTool (requires-action approvals), ItemCardGroup, KPIGroup, Timeline, Segment, PromptInput. HeroUI: Tabs, Chip, ProgressCircle, Slider.

nPlan.text:
Pro: Stepper (vertical), DataGrid, Timeline, CodeBlock, Segment. HeroUI: Tabs, Slider, Card.
app.plan is a defineDoc with history: rewindable. Only the plan_* tools write it, one commit per call. The revision slider reads snapshotAsOf().

nFleet.text:
Pro: KPIGroup/KPI, DataGrid, Widget, Segment. HeroUI: ProgressBar, Chip.
Tool counts and failures come from an afterTool hook. Item-to-item time comes from startedAt/finishedAt on plan items. 'Started as' shows the manager's fresh or fork choice.

nWorker.text:
Pro: KPIGroup (vertical), Timeline, Widget. HeroUI: Tabs, Alert, Chip.
The Transcript and Runtime tasks tabs open the drill-downs below. 'With desk-lead' is the manager-worker channel, kept apart from people's channels.

nChannels.text:
Pro: DataGrid, Segment, Timeline, Widget. HeroUI: Avatar, Switch, Label, Chip.
An inbound message is submit() with entry kind channel.message and a requestId. Chatter is a write and starts no run. The reply tool can only answer a message's origin.

nDx.text: Four extensions on Pi Durable 1.5.2: plan (defineDoc + tools), spawn_worker (tx.createConversation or tx.forkConversation, the manager picks), channel adapters plus a reply tool, and a narrate task on stored sleeps.

rowRules.text: ST1.22: rules in the portal. Where a rule shows, and how a refusal names it (G5, Aaron's 1A 2A 3A 4A)

nRulesThing.text:
Group: a thing's page. Rules sit under the lifecycle, one row per rule (1A). Each row says the rule in one sentence, which fields and states it holds in, and what a caller gets when it breaks.
handle has two rules, each owning a refusal. oneNamePerPerson carries its own written sentence, so its row says so (2A, optional description). profile has one rule that refuses nothing: its row says a break is a defect.
The lifecycle carries no mark for rules (3A); the Errors list says what decides each refusal: a rule, the machine, or the handler.
Pro: Widget, ItemCardGroup, ItemCard. HeroUI: Tabs, Chip. Hooks: rules, rule, rule-sentence, refusal, refusal-sentence, rule-link, lifecycle, operation-row.
Facts from examples/plugged-in/generated: docs/handle/index.md and docs/profile/index.md (rules, sentences), api/src/errors.ts (codes, HTTP status, exit), portal/blueprint.json (states, moves).

nRulesOp.text:
Group: an operation's page. Every refusal a rule owns reads as the rule's sentence and links to the rule's row on the thing's page (2A). The spine gains a rules stop between the move and the commit, only for an operation that can break a rule (4A).
claim can break two rules, so it has the stop. release only leaves claimed, so it has none; the other refusals on both pages have no rule and no link.
Pro: Widget, Timeline, ItemCard. HeroUI: Tabs, Chip. Hooks: refusal, refusal-sentence, rule-link, spine-stop (move, rules, commit).
Facts from examples/plugged-in/generated: docs/handle/claim.md and release.md (refusals, steps, journeys), api/src/errors.ts, portal/blueprint.json (operations.<op>.invariants).
